title: SailPoint Admin Domain 6 questions (6.3)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with SailPoint.

questions.stem: A compliance lead asks what separation of duties means as a control in Identity Security Cloud. Which description is BEST?
choices: Only the source owner may approve access requests for that source's entitlements
Every identity must certify its own access at least once a year
No one person should be able to complete a sensitive process alone
Accounts on a source must all share the same password policy
questions.answer: No one person should be able to complete a sensitive process alone
questions.explanation: SoD means conflicting duties, such as recording and paying invoices, are split between people. Certifications and password policies are separate governance features.

questions.stem: An administrator is reviewing the two kinds of SoD policy that the ISC policy API supports. Which pair names them correctly?
choices: Conflicting access based policies and general (search query based) policies
Role policies and entitlement policies with separate limits
Source policies and identity profile policies
Preventive policies and detective policies, each stored as a separate object type
questions.answer: Conflicting access based policies and general (search query based) policies
questions.explanation: The API types a policy as conflicting access based (two access lists) or general (defined by a search query). Preventive and detective describe how a policy is enforced, not separate policy objects.

questions.stem: An auditor wants a policy that flags identities matching a custom condition expressed as an ISC search query rather than two lists of access. Which policy type fits BEST?
choices: A role with membership criteria that matches the condition
A general policy defined by a search query
A password policy attached to a sync group
A conflicting access based policy with an empty List B
questions.answer: A general policy defined by a search query
questions.explanation: General policies are query based, while conflicting access policies compare List A with List B. A list left empty causes errors, and a role grants access instead of flagging it.

questions.stem: A security admin plans to create many SoD policies for a large ERP rollout. What limit on policies in a single tenant should the admin plan around?
choices: A maximum of 50 policies per source
A maximum of 500 policies in total, of either type
A maximum of 100 enabled policies with no limit on disabled ones
No limit, as long as each policy has an owner
questions.answer: A maximum of 500 policies in total, of either type
questions.explanation: The documented tenant limit is 500 policies combined across both types. The figure of 50 applies to access items per list in an access-based policy, not to the number of policies.

questions.stem: A new team member assumes SoD policies in ISC evaluate service accounts and other machine accounts as well as people. How are SoD policies applied?
choices: They evaluate only accounts on authoritative sources
They evaluate the access held by human identities
They evaluate every account, including machine accounts, equally
They evaluate only uncorrelated accounts on each source
questions.answer: They evaluate the access held by human identities
questions.explanation: The SoD service is described as limiting each human user's involvement in sensitive processes and flagging human identities holding access from both lists. It is not an uncorrelated-account or authoritative-source check.

questions.stem: Which user level, besides a full Admin, is intended for creating and editing SoD policies in Identity Security Cloud?
choices: Helpdesk
SoD Policy Admin
Source Admin
Report Admin
questions.answer: SoD Policy Admin
questions.explanation: Admins and SoD Policy Admins create, edit, enable and schedule SoD policies. Source Admin manages sources and Helpdesk handles identity support tasks.

questions.stem: An admin builds a policy so that people who create vendors cannot also approve vendor payments. How does a conflicting access based policy detect this?
choices: It flags an identity whose manager also holds List B access
It flags an identity holding any access from List A only
It flags an identity whose List A access was granted most recently
It flags an identity holding access from both List A and List B
questions.answer: It flags an identity holding access from both List A and List B
questions.explanation: A conflicting access policy has two named lists, and a violation is raised only when one identity has items from both. Holding items from one list alone is not a conflict.

questions.stem: While adding items to List A of an SoD policy, an admin looks for the kinds of access that can be selected. Which access item types are available?
choices: Entitlements only, because roles are evaluated separately
Applications and governance groups only
Entitlements, access profiles and roles
Sources, identity profiles and lifecycle states
questions.answer: Entitlements, access profiles and roles
questions.explanation: The Add Access Items dialog has tabs for Entitlements, Access Profiles and Roles. Sources, identity profiles and governance groups are not access items for a policy list.

questions.stem: A policy author wants to put 80 finance entitlements on one side of a single SoD policy. What should the author expect?
choices: Each list allows at most 50 access items, so the policy must be split
The list accepts them once a governance group owns the policy
The list accepts them, but only the first ten are evaluated
The list accepts them, because only roles and access profiles count toward a limit
questions.answer: Each list allows at most 50 access items, so the policy must be split
questions.explanation: Access-based SoD policies allow a maximum of 50 access items per side. Splitting the conflict across policies, or grouping access into access profiles or roles, keeps each list under the limit.

questions.stem: An admin saves a draft SoD policy with items in List A but leaves List B empty, planning to fill it later. What is the MOST likely result?
choices: The policy automatically copies List A into List B
The policy runs normally and simply returns no violations until List B is filled
The policy flags everyone holding any List A item
The policy will error until each list has at least one access item
questions.answer: The policy will error until each list has at least one access item
questions.explanation: Documentation states that each access list needs at least one item to prevent errors. With nothing to compare against, the policy cannot evaluate conflicts.

questions.stem: After creating an SoD policy, an auditor wants to read exactly how the rule is defined in plain terms. Where should the auditor look?
choices: The policy's Policy Definition page
The Task Manager of the policy owner
The identity profile mapping page
The Aggregation History page of each source
questions.answer: The policy's Policy Definition page
questions.explanation: The Policy Definition page states the rule, such as identities with List A items cannot also have List B items, and lists every access item. Aggregation history and mappings are unrelated.

questions.stem: A controls analyst designs a purchasing policy. Which pair of access items is the BEST example of an SoD conflict to place on opposite lists?
choices: Read Vendor List and Read Purchase Order
Read Purchase Order and Print Purchase Order
Create Purchase Order and Read Purchase Order
Create Purchase Order and Approve Purchase Order
questions.answer: Create Purchase Order and Approve Purchase Order
questions.explanation: An SoD conflict pairs duties that let one person initiate and authorize the same transaction. Read or print rights combined with each other do not create that risk.

questions.stem: A policy owner wants ISC to automatically cancel any access request that would give a user conflicting access under one specific policy. Which policy setting achieves this?
choices: Disable the policy and schedule a weekly run
Set the policy's access request option to Allow submission
Set the policy risk level to Critical
Set the policy's access request option to Block submission
questions.answer: Set the policy's access request option to Block submission
questions.explanation: Block submission cancels requests that conflict with that policy. Allow submission still lets the request go to approvers, and risk level only classifies violations.

questions.stem: An admin chooses Allow submission on an SoD policy. A user then requests access that conflicts with the policy. What happens?
choices: The request continues and is routed to the configured approvers
The request is held in a queue until the next scheduled run of the policy completes
The request is converted into a certification campaign
The request is cancelled before any approver sees it
questions.answer: The request continues and is routed to the configured approvers
questions.explanation: With Allow submission, conflicting requests are routed to approvers so a person can decide with the conflict in view. Automatic cancellation is the Block submission behaviour.

questions.stem: Leadership wants every ISC access request with any SoD conflict blocked, regardless of individual policy settings. Where should the admin configure this?
choices: Admin > Connections > Sources > Account Management > Account Correlation
Admin > Identity Management > Identity Profiles > Mappings
Admin > Password Mgmt > Sync Groups
Admin > Global > System Settings > Feature Settings > Access Requests
questions.answer: Admin > Global > System Settings > Feature Settings > Access Requests
questions.explanation: The global SoD Conflicts toggles live in the Access Requests feature settings and apply regardless of each policy's own option. The other pages configure sources, mappings and passwords.

questions.stem: An identity governance manager explains the difference between preventive and detective SoD. Which statement describes the preventive side?
choices: Running a policy on a schedule to list violations that already exist in the tenant
Certifying violations in a later campaign
Checking requested access against policies before it is granted
Exporting the violations table for auditors
questions.answer: Checking requested access against policies before it is granted
questions.explanation: Preventive enforcement evaluates an access request before provisioning and can block or flag it. Scheduled runs, certifications and exports find or review violations that already exist.

questions.stem: An SoD policy is set to Block submission, but a user already held both conflicting entitlements before the policy was created. What should the admin expect?
choices: The existing conflict appears as a violation when the policy runs
The policy cannot be enabled until the existing conflict is removed from the user
The conflict is ignored because it predates the policy
The policy removes one of the entitlements automatically
questions.answer: The existing conflict appears as a violation when the policy runs
questions.explanation: Blocking applies to new access requests. Access already held is found by running or scheduling the policy, which lists violations for owners to remediate or mitigate.

questions.stem: A company also uses SAP access request management alongside ISC. The global SoD settings offer a separate toggle for those requests. What does that toggle do?
choices: It sends SAP conflicts to the Helpdesk queue
It disables all SAP sources until conflicts are mitigated
It converts SAP entitlements into access profiles
It blocks SAP ARM access requests that have SoD conflicts
questions.answer: It blocks SAP ARM access requests that have SoD conflicts
questions.explanation: The Access Requests feature settings include one toggle for ISC requests and another for SAP ARM requests with SoD conflicts. Neither disables sources or changes access objects.

questions.stem: An auditor needs an immediate list of current violations for a newly enabled SoD policy. What should the SoD Policy Admin do FIRST?
choices: Run an unoptimized aggregation of every source
Select Actions > Run Policy on the policy
Wait for the nightly identity refresh to evaluate it
Create a new identity profile for the auditors
questions.answer: Select Actions > Run Policy on the policy
questions.explanation: Run Policy evaluates the policy at the next available time and lists violations on the Policy Violations page. Aggregation and identity profiles do not run SoD policies.

questions.stem: A compliance officer wants an SoD policy to run every Monday and email the results to two managers. Which action is designed for this?
choices: A search subscription on the Policy Definition page
Actions > Export, then forward the file each Monday
Actions > Schedule, with a frequency and subscribers
A source aggregation schedule on the finance source
questions.answer: Actions > Schedule, with a frequency and subscribers
questions.explanation: Scheduling a policy sets frequency, times, end date and notification subscribers. Export is a one-time download, and aggregation schedules do not evaluate SoD.

questions.stem: Subscribers to a scheduled SoD policy complain about emails when nothing was found. What can the admin change in the schedule?
choices: Turn off the toggle that sends an email when there are no violations
Remove the policy owner so no emails are sent
Switch the policy's access request option from Block submission to Allow submission
Lower the policy risk level to Low
questions.answer: Turn off the toggle that sends an email when there are no violations
questions.explanation: The schedule includes a toggle for emailing when there are no violations. Owner, risk level and the access request option do not control empty-result emails.

questions.stem: Where can Admins, SoD Violations Admins and SoD Compliance Officers view and filter the list of SoD violations?
choices: Admin > Identity Management > Identity Profiles
Admin > SoD Policies > Policy Violations
Admin > Global > Reports > Uncorrelated Accounts
Admin > Connections > Aggregation Activity
questions.answer: Admin > SoD Policies > Policy Violations
questions.explanation: The Policy Violations page lists violations and filters by policy, identity, violation owner or level, with All, Open and Mitigated quick filters. The other pages concern aggregation, correlation and profiles.

questions.stem: An IAM engineer wants a ticket opened in the ITSM tool whenever a new SoD violation is detected. Which ISC feature is designed for this?
choices: Configuring a password sync group
Subscribing to the SoD Violation Opened event trigger
Setting the policy to Block submission
Adding the ITSM tool's service account as a co-owner of the policy
questions.answer: Subscribing to the SoD Violation Opened event trigger
questions.explanation: SoD event triggers fire on violation lifecycle events, and SoD Violation Opened supports custom notifications or integrations. Ownership and blocking settings do not call external systems.

questions.stem: A policy owner wants reviewers to confirm or revoke the conflicting access found by one SoD policy. Which option on the policy details page supports this directly?
choices: Actions > Delete
Actions > Schedule with no subscribers
Actions > Create Certification
Actions > Disable Policy
questions.answer: Actions > Create Certification
questions.explanation: The policy's Actions menu includes Create Certification so reviewers can act on violators' access. Disabling or deleting the policy hides the problem and can harm compliance evidence.

questions.stem: An SoD policy's Violation Owner is set to None, and no one holds the Violation Admin level. Who is assigned to address violations?
choices: The source owner of List A
The identity's manager
The policy co-owners in turn
An Org Admin
questions.answer: An Org Admin
questions.explanation: With no violation owner and no Violation Admin, ownership falls to an Org Admin. Manager can be chosen explicitly, but it is not the fallback.

questions.stem: A finance clerk must temporarily hold conflicting access during a system migration, and the risk has been accepted. What is the BEST way to record this in ISC?
choices: Lower the policy risk level so it stops reporting
Delete the SoD policy until the migration ends
Mitigate the violation with a mitigating control and comments
Remove the clerk's identity from the identity profile until the migration ends
questions.answer: Mitigate the violation with a mitigating control and comments
questions.explanation: Mitigating a violation applies a control that documents the accepted risk and can expire. Deleting or weakening the policy removes evidence and protection for everyone else.

questions.stem: An admin is creating a mitigating control for SoD exceptions. Which setting ensures accepted exceptions are reviewed again rather than lasting forever?
choices: The policy's tags
The number of days before the control expires
The policy's List B name
The policy's External Reference URL
questions.answer: The number of days before the control expires
questions.explanation: Controls include an expiration in days, so mitigations lapse and are reconsidered. Reference URLs, tags and list names are descriptive only.

questions.stem: A violation is raised on a policy whose level is High. What risk level does the violation itself carry?
choices: No level, because only policies carry levels
Low, until an owner reviews it
Critical, because all violations start at the top level
High, because violations inherit the policy's level
questions.answer: High, because violations inherit the policy's level
questions.explanation: Violations inherit the risk level of the policy they violate. That lets owners filter and prioritise violations by level.

questions.stem: Which user level can create and edit SoD controls, other than a full Admin?
choices: SoD Controls Admin
SoD Compliance Officer
Access Profile Admin
Cert Admin
questions.answer: SoD Controls Admin
questions.explanation: Admins and SoD Controls Admins manage mitigating controls. SoD Compliance Officers can view violations, and Cert Admins run certifications.

questions.stem: When defining a policy, an admin fills in Mitigation Advice and Remediation Advice. What purpose do these fields serve?
choices: They set how many days a violation stays open
They decide which approvers receive conflicting requests
They guide owners on how to handle violations of the policy
They choose which sources the policy evaluates
questions.answer: They guide owners on how to handle violations of the policy
questions.explanation: Advice fields give violation handlers guidance on mitigating or remediating conflicts. Approval routing and expiry come from other settings.

questions.stem: A violation owner wants a quick way to reach the open violations assigned to them. What does ISC provide?
choices: A line in the Aggregation History of each source
A tile on MySailPoint that opens their open violations
A banner on each source configuration page
A weekly CSV attached to the source owner email
questions.answer: A tile on MySailPoint that opens their open violations
questions.explanation: Violation owners can use a MySailPoint tile to reach violations they own. Source banners and aggregation history report source health, not SoD work.

questions.stem: A help desk manager wants the same password applied across Active Directory and two other direct connect sources whenever a user changes it. Which ISC feature does this?
choices: An identity profile with three authoritative sources
A delta aggregation schedule on each source
A password sync group
An SoD policy with the three sources in List A
questions.answer: A password sync group
questions.explanation: Sync groups combine direct connect sources so a password change applies across them. SoD policies and identity profiles do not change passwords.

questions.stem: An admin is creating a password sync group. Which prerequisite is required?
choices: At least two direct connect sources set up for password management and a password policy
A governance group that owns every source in the group
At least one flat file source and one SoD policy
One authoritative source with delta aggregation enabled and a governance group as its owner
questions.answer: At least two direct connect sources set up for password management and a password policy
questions.explanation: Sync groups need at least two direct connect sources set up for password management, an access application on each authentication source, and a password policy. Flat file sources cannot have passwords set.

questions.stem: An admin wants to stop users choosing common words as passwords. Where is a password dictionary enabled?
choices: In the SoD policy rules under Admin > SoD Policies > Policy Definition
In the source's Account Correlation settings
In a password policy under Admin > Password Mgmt > Policies
In the identity profile's lifecycle states
questions.answer: In a password policy under Admin > Password Mgmt > Policies
questions.explanation: The password dictionary is a password policy option. SoD rules, correlation and lifecycle states do not govern password content.

questions.stem: An admin deletes a password sync group that used a strict policy. What happens to the password policy for the sources that were in the group?
choices: The sources are disabled until a new group is created
The sources revert to having no password policy at all
The policy is deleted along with the group
The policy becomes assigned directly to those sources
questions.answer: The policy becomes assigned directly to those sources
questions.explanation: After a sync group is deleted, its policy is assigned directly to the associated sources and their passwords become independent. The policy is not deleted.

questions.stem: Before adding several sources to one sync group, what should the admin verify about the chosen password policy?
choices: That its rules are acceptable to every source in the group
That it has no exceptions configured
That it is the most recently created policy
That it matches the identity profile priority order
questions.answer: That its rules are acceptable to every source in the group
questions.explanation: If the policy allows passwords that one source rejects, users see errors changing passwords in the group. The policy must satisfy all member sources.

questions.stem: Match each Identity Security Cloud policy feature to what it does.

pairs.match: Flags identities holding items from both List A and List B
Flags identities matched by a search query
Sets complexity rules for passwords on sources
Records an accepted, expiring exception to a violation

targets_extra: Assigns access automatically when membership criteria match
questions.explanation: Access-based and query-based policies detect SoD conflicts, password policies govern password strength and controls document accepted risk. Automatic assignment by criteria describes roles, not policies.

questions.stem: Put the steps for creating a conflicting access SoD policy in order.
items: Go to Admin > SoD Policies and select Create New
Enter policy details, owners, violation owner and access request option
Name List A and add its access items
Name List B and add its access items
Review the policy, finish and enable it
questions.explanation: Details and ownership come first, then the two conflicting lists, then review. The policy must be enabled before it is applied.

questions.stem: An admin wants conflicting access requests stopped before approval. Which TWO configurations do this?
choices: Turn on the global toggle to block ISC access requests with SoD conflicts
Assign a mitigating control with a short expiration
Set the individual policy's access request option to Block submission
Schedule the policy to run daily with subscribers
Set the individual policy's access request option to Allow submission
answers: Set the individual policy's access request option to Block submission
Turn on the global toggle to block ISC access requests with SoD conflicts
questions.explanation: Per-policy Block submission and the global blocking toggle both cancel conflicting requests. Allow submission routes them to approvers, and schedules or controls act after access exists.
